Cluster Split

Source: R/cluster.R
cluster_split.Rd

Cluster Split splits data into groups based on taxomic group. It then clusters them using the following methods: opticluster, average neighbor, nearest neighbor, furthest neighbor, and weighted neighbor. You can read more about [cluster split](https://mothur.org/wiki/cluster.split/) on the mothur wiki.

Usage

cluster_split(
  fasta,
  taxonomy,
  count_table,
  cluster_method,
  cutoff,
  taxonomy_cutoff,
  feature_column_name = "feature",
  bin_column_name = "bin",
  random_seed = 123,
  delta = 1e-04,
  max_iterations = 100,
  initialize = "singleton",
  metric = "mcc",
  pairwise_distance_method = "onegap",
  number_of_threads = 1,
  strollur_object = NULL
)

Arguments

fasta

a`data.frame` representation of your fasta data. This can be generated using the `read_fasta` function. The fasta `data.frame` must contain two columns: sequence_name and sequence.

taxonomy

a`data.frame` representation of your taxonomy data. This can be generated using the `read_mothur_taxonomy` function. The taxonomy `data.frame` must contain two columns: sequence_name and taxonomy.

count_table

the count table that represents the data, must be read using the `read_count()` function.

cluster_method

the clustering method you wish to use. Your clustering options are: opticluster, average neighbor, nearest neighbor, furthest neighbor, and weighted neighbor.

cutoff

a `numerical` value that represents the distance cutoff.

taxonomy_cutoff

a `integer` value that represents the taxonomic level cutoff.

feature_column_name

Set the name of the column in the cluster dataframe that contains the sequence names. This is a `character` value.

bin_column_name

Set the name of the column in the cluster dataframe that contains the name of the group of sequence names. This is a `character` value.

random_seed

a `integer` value that represents the current random seed.

delta

Allows you to set the stable value for the metric in the opticluster method. It defaults to 0.0001, to reach full convergence set this value to 0.

max_iterations

the max amount of iterations the opticluster method will run. The default is 100.

initialize

this parameter allows you to set the default randomization of for the opticluster method. The two methods are: "singleton" and "oneotu." Singleton will randomly assign each sequence to its own OTU while "oneotu" assigns all sequence into one OTU. Defaults to singleton.

metric

this parameter allows you to choose which metric the cluster will optimize to, the options are: Matthews correlation coefficient (mcc), sensitivity (sens), specificity (spec), true positives + true negatives (tptn), false positives + false negatives (fpfn), true positives (tp), true negative (tn), false positive (fp), false negative (fn), f1score (f1score), accuracy (accuracy), positive predictive value (ppv), negative predictive value (npv), false discovery rate (fdr). The default metric is mcc.

pairwise_distance_method

the method you wish to use to calculate pairwise distances between aligned sequences. As of current we only allow the calculation of fasta sequences, and the current methods are; onegap, nogap, and eachgap. For more information look at the (mother webpage)[https://mothur.org/wiki/dist.seqs/]. This is a `character` value.

number_of_threads

a `integer` value that represents the amount of allotted threads that can be used.

strollur_object

Using the `strollur` r package, you can use your created strollur object to save your clustering results to. This allows you to seamless modify your strollur object and analysis results as needed.

Value

A list of `data.frames` that contain abundance, and clustering results.

Examples


 cutoff <- 0.2
 count_table <- read_count(example_path("amazon.full.count_table"))
 fasta <- read_fasta(example_path("amazon.align"))
 taxonomy <- read_mothur_taxonomy(example_path("amazon.taxonomy"))
 df <- cluster_split(fasta, taxonomy, count_table, "opti",
                     cutoff, 3, number_of_threads = 1)
